name: regulation and standards
reason: Regulation factors with no artefact beyond the published instruments. Ten entries in D24 now operationalise the parts a system owner can actually check; the rest of the lens is still text with no procedure, and the Class III organisational facts stay unavailable.

L13-025.note: Two frameworks read against one control set is the interpretation divergence question.

L13-001.note: Scope of a test, with the written scope as the artefact and the signed authority as the check.

L13-005.note: The charging guidance is what makes the statute breadth concrete enough to plan against.

L13-002.note: Written authorisation, verified by who signed it rather than whether a document exists.

L13-003.note: Third party hosting terms, checked before the test rather than after.

L13-007.note: The 72 hour clock, with the awareness timestamp as the oracle.

L13-008.note: Recipient set, tested by listing who a real incident would have to be told.

L13-009.note: Reportable versus recordable, decided against article 33(5) and recorded.

L13-011.note: Access requests, tested against what each store can actually answer from.

L13-012.note: Erasure feasibility, with every store named including backups.

L13-013.note: Retention versus minimisation, resolved per store rather than per policy.

L13-014.note: A hold flag that suspends the deletion job, with a deletion during a hold as the failure signal.

L13-015.note: Consent records mapped to processing activities through a privacy profile.

L13-016.note: Withdrawal propagation, checked against the mapping rather than assumed.

L13-017.note: Processing basis documented per activity, with unmapped activities listed.

L13-018.note: Whether card data enters the environment at all, which is the scope question.

L13-019.note: Tokenisation coverage, tested by searching every store for a primary account number.

L13-020.note: The cardholder data environment boundary, compared against observed flows.

L13-026.note: Standard version attached to the compliance claim, read from the certificate.

L13-027.note: Certification scope, checked against the system in question rather than a sibling.

L13-028.note: Assessor independence, recorded with the engagement.

L13-029.note: Self attestation, identified as such rather than presented as verification.

L13-030.note: Cryptographic distribution obligations, classified by destination.

L13-034.note: Screening recorded at onboarding and re-screened on the list cadence.

L13-038.note: Contractual security promises, checked against the control set rather than the brochure.

L13-046.note: Embargo period, stated and honoured on a real report.

L13-047.note: Bounty terms, read for a testing licence and a promise not to sue.

L13-006.note: The guidance's own categories mapped against the scope is the practical good faith test.

L13-010.note: Transfer restriction as a data governance question, checked against the processing map.

L13-022.note: Age basis and children's data constraints under the same decision framework.

L13-023.note: Record keeping obligations are what a regulator's own form asks for.

L13-041.note: Each decision point classified as automated or human is the restriction test.

L13-042.note: Profiling disclosure follows from the same classification.

L13-048.note: The remedy route and timeline is what makes a terms prohibition actionable.

L13-052.note: Which regime applies by data subject location is the guidance's own scope question.

L13-054.note: A sector regulator's route and deadline, read from its own reporting page.

L13-058.note: Licence obligations mapped to what distribution does is the disclosure duty.

L13-059.note: The complaint evidence and timeline is the trademark remedy.

L13-063.note: A public profile is itself documentation that reveals which controls exist.

L13-064.note: Reading current enforcement material is how direction change is detected.

L13-004.note: What may be retained, where and for how long, applied and checked at close.

L13-024.note: Downgraded from L2: The purple loop entry tests whether a detection fires, not whether the application's own audit trail is tamper evident. Those are different artefacts and I had already downgraded this once for the same reason. The concept is named and no procedure for it is stated.

L13-050.note: Retention stated and still retrievable at its end is the evidentiary standard.

L13-051.note: Handler and time of each transfer recorded is chain of custody.

L13-056.note: A source's licence recorded against its use is the due diligence question.

L13-057.note: Reporting an exploited flaw is the same disclosure path as a vendor report.

L13-036.note: Platform terms as a control is read from the terms themselves, which is what the entry points at.

L13-055.note: Designation status read from the regulator's list rather than assumed.

L13-035.note: An availability window the test must respect is the accessibility-as-constraint case.

L13-031.note: Release without dual control, and the instrument recorded, covers lawful access.

L13-032.note: The request type recorded so a subpoena and a warrant are distinguishable is the distinction.

L13-033.note: An aggregate count published is the transparency obligation.

L13-053.note: A cross border request is the same instrument verification path.

L13-049.note: The signature standard cited, and whether the jurisdiction recognises it.
